transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

What finally brought me in is I just don’t feel like myself anymore. I used to paint, go hiking, sing in choir, see my family on Sundays… and now, even if I have free time, I just sit there. I can’t seem to care enough to do any of it.
How long have you been feeling this way—unable to enjoy or care about the things you used to do?
It’s been building for about eight months now, since I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum initiative.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks or months of low mood and loss of interest—at any earlier point in your life?
I’m not sure. I can’t think of another time it lasted like this.
Besides the loss of interest, have you noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels over these past eight months?

My sleep has been really disrupted. I lie awake going over grant details in my head, then wake up around three or four in the morning. And even if I sleep later, I wake up feeling like I didn’t rest at all.
Have you noticed anything like hearing voices or sounds others don't seem to hear, or having thoughts or beliefs that others have told you seem unusual or out of the ordinary?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that. I don’t hear things other people don’t, and no one’s told me my thoughts or beliefs seem unusual.
Over these past eight months, would you say you've felt sad, down, or empty most of the day, nearly every day—even on days when things at work aren't actively stressful?
Yes. Most days it feels like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. Even when I’m in class with the students, or at home with my husband, I still feel hollow and like I could cry.
Aside from the work situation, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like your health, finances, or family—and having a hard time controlling that worry?
I’m not really sure. It’s mostly the work situation that keeps running through my mind.
Do you notice this heavy, hollow feeling even during moments when you're not thinking about or dealing with the work situation—like on a weekend trip or during a hobby you used to enjoy?

Yes. Even when I’m not dealing with work, it’s still there. I can be at home with my husband or around the students, and I just feel hollow, like I’m close to crying. Everything has this heavy, gray feeling to it.

Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, or found yourself taking on projects or spending money more impulsively than normal?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed periods where I felt unusually energized or needed much less sleep, or anything like that.
Have you had any thoughts of death, or thoughts that you'd be better off not being here, during this time?

Sometimes, late at night in the studio, I think it might be a relief if I just didn’t wake up. I haven’t made any plan, but it scares me. I told my husband because I didn’t feel like I could handle those thoughts by myself anymore.

Over these past eight months, has this hollow, heavy feeling made it difficult or impossible for you to keep up with your usual work and daily responsibilities, or have you still been able to manage most of your day-to-day tasks despite feeling this way?

It’s made it hard to keep up. I’ve missed several teaching sessions, and I’ve been avoiding the student workshops because I just can’t handle the responsibilities the way I used to. At home, my husband has had to do more too. I pull away from family plans, and I don’t really feel safe trying to push through it on my own.
